lead: With all generators offline, the battery is the only source; it carries essential loads until another source comes online. A 24 V lead-acid battery has 12 cells at about 2.1 V each. A 24 V nickel-cadmium battery has 19 or 20 cells at about 1.25 V each. Aircraft use these batteries for starting, emergency DC buses and standby instruments. Only a few universities teach the chemistry and testing detail; the comparison is standard.
prereq: You need Chapter 3.1 and Chapter 3.2, because the battery sits on the DC bus and is charged through a TRU or dedicated charger.

sections.h3: Lead-acid: 12 cells, sulphuric acid, specific gravity

blocks.text: A lead-acid cell has a lead-dioxide positive plate, a sponge-lead negative plate and dilute sulphuric acid electrolyte. Each cell gives about 2.1 V on load; twelve in series give 24 V. Specific gravity near 1.28 at full charge shows state of charge, because charging raises acid concentration. Read it after the battery rests or after mixing; water added during topping up lowers the reading until it mixes.

Lead-acid gives strong cranking current and is cheap, but heavy per ampere-hour. Deep discharge damages the plates. Capacity is in ampere-hours (Ah): Ah = I × t, where I is current in amperes and t is time in hours. C-rate = I ÷ rated Ah; a 40 Ah battery at 40 A is 1C, the 1-hour rate. The figure plots terminal voltage against capacity discharged at 1C. Lead-acid voltage falls steadily, so the end point is easy to see.

sections.h3: Nickel-cadmium: 19 or 20 cells, flat voltage, thermal risk

blocks.text: A nickel-cadmium (NiCd) cell uses nickel hydroxide positive and cadmium negative plates in potassium hydroxide electrolyte. Sintered plates pack active material into a porous nickel matrix. Each cell gives about 1.25 V, so 19 cells give 23.75 V and 20 cells give 25 V; both are called 24 V batteries. Never use a 12-cell lead-acid charger setting on a NiCd battery.

NiCd has low internal resistance, good cold performance and long life. Its voltage stays almost flat until nearly discharged, so a simple voltage reading is a poor state-of-charge check. The flat curve also means the end point must be detected carefully. NiCd is prone to thermal runaway: high temperature raises charging current, which raises temperature further and can vent electrolyte. It also shows voltage depression, often called memory effect, after repeated partial discharge and overcharge; a full slow discharge and recharge restores most capacity.

A capacity check discharges the battery at constant current to a stated end voltage, records Ah removed, and compares it with rated Ah. A 40 Ah battery that gives only 30 Ah has 75% capacity. Lead-acid charges at constant current, then at constant voltage (float) to avoid overcharge. Nickel-cadmium is charged at constant current, stopped by voltage or temperature cut-off. Never leave a NiCd on a constant-voltage charge: its cell voltage falls as it heats, so current keeps rising. Deep discharge below the end voltage damages both types.
Depth of discharge (DoD) = (Ah removed ÷ rated Ah) × 100%. In the worked example, 20 Ah from a 40 Ah battery is 50% DoD. The remaining 20 Ah at 20 A lasts 1 hour if rate effects are ignored.

Some syllabi also list lithium-ion. It gives more energy per kilogram and a flatter voltage than lead-acid or NiCd, but it needs a battery management system because overcharge or cell damage can cause fire. That fire risk is why lithium needs stricter charge control and temperature monitoring.

figure.caption: At 1C, lead-acid settles from 25.2 V to 21.4 V; nickel-cadmium stays near 24.5 V until about 90% and then falls to 21.0 V.

spec.aria: The nickel-cadmium curve stays almost flat until about ninety percent discharge and then falls sharply, while the lead-acid voltage falls steadily from the start.

examples.question: A 24 V lead-acid battery is rated 40 Ah at the 1-hour rate. It supplies 40 A for 30 minutes. (a) How many ampere-hours are used? (b) What is the depth of discharge? (c) If the load then drops to 20 A, how long will the remaining charge last?
steps: Ah used = I × t = 40 A × 0.5 h = 20 Ah.
examples.answer: 20 Ah is used, the depth of discharge is 50%, and the remaining charge lasts 1 hour at 20 A, ignoring rate effects.
examples.check:
c = 40.0
i = 40.0
t_h = 0.5
ah_used = i * t_h
dod = ah_used / c * 100
remaining = c - ah_used
t2 = remaining / 20.0
print(int(ah_used))
print(int(dod))
print(int(t2))

code.code:
c = 40.0
i = 40.0
t = 0.5
ah = i * t
print(int(ah))
print(int(ah / c * 100))
print(int((c - ah) / 20.0))

traps: Do not assume a 24 V NiCd battery has 12 cells; it has 19 or 20 cells.
Do not take a specific-gravity reading just after topping up with water; the acid is diluted until mixing.
Do not read 40 Ah as a continuous 40 A rating; it is 40 A for 1 hour at the 1-hour rate.
Do not call every NiCd capacity loss memory effect; voltage depression and overcharge also reduce capacity.
Do not use open-circuit voltage alone for NiCd state of charge; its curve is flat.

quiz.q: How many cells make a 24 V lead-acid and a 24 V NiCd battery?
quiz.a: 12 lead-acid cells at about 2.1 V; 19 or 20 NiCd cells at about 1.25 V.

quiz.q: Why is specific gravity used on lead-acid batteries?
quiz.a: It indicates state of charge because charging changes acid concentration; near 1.28 means full charge.

quiz.q: A 30 Ah battery at the 1-hour rate supplies 15 A for 48 minutes. Find Ah used and depth of discharge.
Explain thermal runaway in a NiCd battery.
quiz.a: High temperature increases charging current, which increases temperature; without temperature sensing the cell can vent.
Discharge current divided by rated Ah; 40 A from a 40 Ah battery is 1C.

quiz.q: Why is terminal voltage a poor NiCd state-of-charge check?
quiz.a: Its voltage stays almost flat until nearly empty, so a small voltage change covers a large capacity change.

beyond: Not for the exam. Battery management systems now estimate state of health from current, voltage and temperature, not from specific gravity. Lithium iron phosphate is replacing some NiCd emergency batteries because it avoids cadmium and has a flatter voltage, but thermal propagation tests remain strict. Search for battery management system, state of health and thermal runaway propagation next.
